title: Chapter 3 Quiz 4
description: Giving values to variables and calculating with + - * / DIV MOD.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Which symbol **gives a value** to a variable?
questions.explanation: The assignment is written VariableName ← Expression. Watch out: = is a comparison, not an assignment.

questions.question: What does **Total ← Total + Pay** do?
options: Displays Total after adding Pay to it
Compares Total with the sum of Total and Pay
Sets Pay to the old value of Total
Replaces Total by the old Total plus Pay
questions.explanation: The right side is calculated first, then the result is stored in Total. Watch out: it is not an equation. Total cannot equal Total + Pay.

questions.question: What is 17 DIV 5? (integer division)
questions.explanation: 17 = 5 × 3 + 2, so the integer quotient is 3. Watch out: DIV gives the quotient, MOD gives the remainder.

questions.question: What is 17 MOD 5? (remainder)
questions.explanation: 17 = 5 × 3 + 2, so the remainder is 2. Watch out: MOD is the remainder, not the quotient.

questions.question: What is 20 MOD 4?
questions.explanation: 4 divides 20 exactly, so the remainder is 0. Watch out: an exact division leaves a remainder of 0, not 4.

questions.question: What is 7 / 2 with the real division?
questions.explanation: The / operator gives a real result: 3.5. Watch out: with DIV the answer would be 3.

questions.question: Match each operator to its meaning.
questions.explanation: These are the arithmetic operators of the course.

questions.question: x ← 10. Then x ← x + 5, then x ← x * 2. What is x?
questions.explanation: 10 + 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30. Watch out: each line uses the value left by the line before.

questions.question: Trace this program: a ← 5, b ← 3, then a ← a + b, b ← a - b, a ← a - b. Fill in the values.
questions.explanation: The three lines swap the two values without a temporary variable. Watch out: a changes first, so b ← a - b uses the new a.

questions.question: This should swap a and b with a temporary variable. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Let a ← 5
Let b ← 3
Let temp ← a
a ← b
b ← a
Display(a, b)
questions.explanation: After a ← b, the old value of a is only kept in temp, so b must receive temp. Watch out: b ← a would copy the new a and both variables would hold 3.

questions.question: This should display the quotient and then the remainder of a divided by b. Two lines have an error.
questions.code:
Read(a, b)
Let q ← a MOD b
Let r ← a DIV b
Display(q, r)
questions.explanation: The quotient needs DIV and the remainder needs MOD, so lines 2 and 3 are swapped. Watch out: both lines look right at first glance.
